title: Diwali Train Rush From Ahmedabad: Sold Out, Long Waitlists, Your Options
excerpt: Festival-season tickets on Ahmedabad-origin trains are gone within minutes of opening, with a booking-scam complaint now flagging suspicious bulk bookings — here's what passengers can actually do.
body:
• Diwali falls on November 8 this year, with Chhath Puja from November 13 to 16 — and trains out of Ahmedabad toward UP, Bihar, Delhi and the north are already fully booked, with waiting lists and IRCTC "Regret" statuses.
  • A complaint to senior Railway authorities alleges seats on Gujarat-origin trains — including the Sabarmati–Jammu Tawi, Ashram, Yoga and Sabarmati Rajdhani — were bulk-blocked under dummy names and sold as "guaranteed confirmed" Diwali packages. Do not buy from unauthorized agents.
  • Railways has announced 43 pairs of trains making 1,053 festival special trips across 13 zones from October 1 to November 30; the Ahmedabad–Darbhanga Special is extended to November 27 and the Ahmedabad–Mumbai Central TOD Special runs to November 26.
  • Your playbook: book the minute the 60-day window opens at 8 AM on IRCTC or the Rail One app, keep UPI/IRCTC wallet ready, complete Aadhaar verification, and keep alternative trains and dates ready.

The crunch

Travelers trying to get home from Ahmedabad for Diwali are discovering that confirmed train berths vanished within minutes of opening. The fight for tickets is fiercest on routes like Ahmedabad–Patna, Delhi–Patna, Mumbai–Patna and Delhi–Gorakhpur, where regular trains now show long waiting lists — or outright "Regret" — on IRCTC. On some services, confirmation chances from the waiting list are virtually nil.

Booking itself has been painful: IRCTC's window opens at 8 AM under the 60-day Advance Reservation Period, but passengers report errors for roughly 10 minutes — by which time seats have moved to waiting-list status — and IRCTC handled over 20 lakh bookings in a single day during the rush.

Context & Background

This is India's largest annual passenger migration compressed into a few weeks. Anticipating the rush, Railways announced 43 pairs of trains making 1,053 festival special trips between October 1 and November 30, 2026, operated across 13 railway zones. The services connect major cities — Kolkata, Prayagraj, Kanpur Central, New Delhi, Palwal, Anand Vihar Terminal and others — and passengers can also use the festival special trains as the main fallback when regular trains are full.

Around Ahmedabad, the division has added targeted capacity: the Ahmedabad–Darbhanga Special has been extended to November 27 specifically for the Diwali and Chhath Puja rush, while the Ahmedabad–Mumbai Central TOD Special runs from September 10 to November 26 across the Navratri–Diwali–Chhath period. On key intercity routes, the crunch is stark — the Sampoorna Kranti Express showed "No Room" in economy for November 1–4 with waiting lists in sleeper and AC three-tier through November 8, and long 3AC waiting lists were reported on the Tejas Rajdhani. Reported Delhi–Patna airfares near ₹20,000 one way for early November underline that flying is no cheap escape hatch.

Impact & Analysis

The Ahmedabad picture carries an extra warning. A complaint submitted to senior Railway authorities in Delhi alleges a booking scam on Gujarat-origin trains ahead of Diwali: seats allegedly blocked in advance under dummy or fictitious names, then handed to real travelers shortly before departure — often after passengers were told their original bookings "could not be confirmed" and offered "guaranteed confirmed" tickets as part of Diwali travel packages. The complaint names the Sabarmati–Jammu Tawi Express, Hapa–Katra Express, Jamnagar–Katra Express, Sarvodaya Express, JAT Vivek Express, Sabarmati–Katra Express, Gandhinagar Capital–Daulatpur Chowk Express, Ashram Express, Yoga Express, Sabarmati–New Delhi Rajdhani and Sabarmati–Banaras Superfast, estimating 100–120 sleeper and 30–40 AC seats per train suspiciously booked for travel between November 5 and 15, plus bulk bookings of around 60 seats on the Rajdhani.

Full details of the booking-scam allegations on Ahmedabad-origin trains raise identity-verification questions as well. The practical lesson: no tour operator has a special Diwali quota. Book only through IRCTC, the Rail One app, or authorized counters — and never travel on a ticket bearing someone else's name.

Diaspora Angle

Many diaspora travelers flying into Ahmedabad for Diwali will still need onward train connections — and the same crunch applies to them. Book through IRCTC or the Rail One app (an account and Aadhaar verification set up in advance make the 8 AM window winnable), target the festival special trains rather than only the flagship Rajdhani services, and build in a buffer day or two around the special-train schedules. And the Ahmedabad-specific caution matters: buy tickets only through official channels, no matter how tempting an agent's "guaranteed berth" pitch sounds.

What's Next

Railway zones say they are monitoring demand and will add extra coaches and more special trips where feasible — watch for announcements of additional festival services in the coming days. A booking checklist for the festive rush can improve your odds: log in before 8 AM, prepare passenger details in advance, keep payment ready, and have alternative trains and dates on standby. For Diwali-week travel, the window is closing fast — what is not booked now will likely only get harder.
